q-904.name: Question 1
q-904.problem: Find $|z|$ if $z=-c-d\text{i},$ where $c$ and $d$ are real numbers.
q-904.worked_solution:
For a complex number $z=a+b\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.
$$

For the complex number $z=-c-d\text{i},$ we have $a=-c$ and $b=-d.$ So, the magnitude is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}|-c-d\text{i}| & =\sqrt{(-c)^{2}+(-d)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{c}^{2}+{d}^{2}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-70259.name: Question 2
q-70259.problem: What is the magnitude of the number $z=3\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}?$
q-70259.worked_solution:
The imaginary number $3\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}$ is equivalent to the complex number $z=0+3\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}.$

We know that for a complex number $z=a+b\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.
$$

So, the magnitude of $z=0+3\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|z| & =\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(3\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The imaginary number 32i is equivalent to the complex number z=0+32i.

q-160280.name: Question 3
q-160280.problem: What is the magnitude of the number $z=-9\text{i}?$
q-160280.worked_solution:
The imaginary number $-9\text{i}$ is equivalent to the complex number $z=0-9\text{i}.$

We know that for a complex number $z=a+b\text{i},$ the magnitude of $z$ is given by

$$
|z|=\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}.
$$

So, the magnitude of $z=0-9\text{i}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|z| & =\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(-9)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{81} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
